<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b16ee8ba069d00bc00d01295869c1036fc9ea2e2` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `76fde58e651c2fd8897fba95e8bb38c24aee39f5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts + packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts (`fieldClausesForTerm`, `neverHoldsText`, `expandSearchToFilter`), packages/spec/src/data/filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts (`textOperatorDoorVerdict`, `TEXT_OPERATOR_DOOR_REFUSED_TYPES`), packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (the class sets), packages/objectql/src/search-companion.ts (`resolveSearchCompanionSources`), all read on `main` `e832ddb1`

Inputs read: card #29546 body + its 3 comments (triage, claim, os-dev-report); PR #29584 body, file list (3 files), net diff against the merge-base `ff827bcf`; check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **No accept set moves — right.** The diff against the merge-base touches two comment blocks and adds one changeset. `resolveSearchFieldResolution`'s body, `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`, `SEARCH_AUTO_EXCLUDED_TYPES` and every test assertion are byte-identical to `main`. The CONTROL case still asserts `{ allowed: ['project_id', 'payload'], source: 'declared' }`.
- **"A declared `json` column is admitted but contributes no clause" — right against the live code.** `fieldClausesForTerm` on `main` returns `[]` when `neverHoldsText(meta)`, which is `textOperatorDoorVerdict(...) === 'door-refusal'`; `json` is in `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES`, which `TEXT_OPERATOR_DOOR_REFUSED_TYPES` spreads. Admission is unmoved: the declared branch filters only by existence and `isVirtualSearchField` (`formula`).
- **"A single-valued `lookup` becomes an `$icontains` over the stored foreign key" — right, and the `$contains` → `$icontains` correction is right.** `lookup` sits in `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` (door verdict `passes`), is not in `SEARCHABLE_ENUM_TYPES` (`select` only), and is not multi-valued unless `multiple: true`, so it falls to the function's final `{ [field]: { $icontains: term } }`. The old text's `$contains` has been wrong since #7641 (the module header on `main` says so in as many words). The "single-valued" qualifier is load-bearing: a `lookup` declared `multiple: true` takes the #21009 membership branch (`$contains`) instead, and the docblock keeps it.
- **"A set made only of such columns answers no rows: never an error, never every row" — right.** `expandSearchToFilter` only answers `null` (the #24284 `INVALID_FIELD` refusal upstream) on an EMPTY resolved set; a non-empty never-text set yields `{ $or: [] }` per term, FALSE under `FILTER_LOGIC_CASES`. The `__search` companion cannot rescue such a set: `resolveSearchCompanionSources` only ever names the display field when its type is in `TITLE_ELIGIBLE_TYPES` (text-family), and `companionWithinSearchFields` requires that source to be inside the set, so a set of never-text columns never carries the companion arm.
- **The door's class list in the docblock (numeric, boolean, calendar-date, instant, clock-time, structured-JSON, plus a `formula` by readable `returnType`) — matches `TEXT_OPERATOR_DOOR_TYPE_CLASSES` and `textOperatorDoorVerdict`'s `formula` branch exactly.** The relative path `./filter-text-operator-declared-type` is right (same directory). `expandSearchToFilter` exists under that name in `@objectstack/objectql` (`search-filter.ts`, imported by `engine.ts`).
- **Public surface:** the docblock sits on an exported function re-exported through `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts` (`export * from './search-fields'`), and `@objectstack/spec`'s build emits `dist/data/index.d.ts` via tsup `BUILD_DTS`, which preserves TSDoc. The published `.d.ts` text therefore changes; nothing a type-checker or runtime consumer reads changes.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **patch**, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset — **right**. AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist 3: a changeset for anything that publishes; `skip-changeset` is only for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package. The docblock ships in the package's `.d.ts`, so a patch is the correct level and the dev's deviation from the card's "no changeset unless the gate asks" is the standard winning over the order, as the report says. `Check Changeset` on the head: success. The triage's "not published text: no `.describe()` moves" was about the `/meta/types` surface, not the `.d.ts`; both are true at once. The changeset body states the four points the docblock makes and nothing more.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` — nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, changeset added against the order: answered above (right).
- Dev flag, Human Minimum 3 unchecked (repo-wide `pnpm lint` left to CI): `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` report success on the head; the remaining lint and type-check runs were still `in_progress` at review time with no failure recorded. A comment-only diff on two files carries no lint risk the scoped runs would not already have surfaced.
- Dev out-of-scope finding, `packages/lint/src/validate-searchable-fields.ts` docblock (~L95-L100 on `main`) still says a declared json column is "a `$contains` over the stored JSON text ... a scan that CAN match": confirmed on `main`. Outside this card's file surface; the seat should carry it as a follow-up card, since the linter's docblock is the second place an author reads this rule.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally: left to CI; not a derived family a comment-only diff can move.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts` — judged against the card's Wanted and the code it cites. The declared-branch text now says exactly what the card asked: never-string-capable types are admitted, contribute no clause, a set made only of them answers no rows, and only "no column at all" is refused. Every claim checked above against `search-filter.ts` and `textOperatorDoorVerdict` on `main` holds. The test comment makes the same reading over a fixture (`project_id: lookup`, `payload: json`) where it is literally true.

Tried to break it:

- Could a reader take "a `formula` whose readable `returnType` names one ... contributes NO clause" as "a formula is admitted to the set"? The sentence sits inside a paragraph about what an ADMITTED column contributes, but Filter 2 two paragraphs up says a `formula` entry is dropped before admission (`SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES` is exactly `formula`). The formula mention is copied from the objectql module header, where it is the door's rule at the expansion seam; in THIS function's docblock it describes a type that never reaches the expansion through the declared branch. Not false (a dropped formula trivially contributes no clause), and the `objectql` header is the one that matters for the auto-default path, so a **should-fix**, not a must-fix.
- Could a multi-valued `lookup` make the test comment's unqualified "`lookup` becomes an `$icontains`" wrong? Only for `multiple: true`, which the fixture does not declare; the docblock carries the qualifier. Nit, folded into should-fix 2.

**Must-fix: none.**

**Should-fix** (none blocks; fold into a follow-up or a later touch of the same docblock):

1. `search-fields.ts` docblock, the `[#29394]` bullet: mark the `formula` case as unreachable on this branch, e.g. "plus a `formula` whose readable `returnType` names one — though Filter 2 drops a `formula` entry before it gets here", or drop the formula parenthetical and leave the door's class list to `filter-text-operator-declared-type`. As written, the admitted-column paragraph names a type the same docblock says is never admitted.
2. The same docblock still says `$contains` where it means "a substring scan" in two unchanged lines (Filter 2: "no stored column for `$contains` to scan"; `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`' note at ~L92: "a `$contains` scan has nothing to look at"), while the corrected bullet now names `$icontains`. Harmless as a generic word, but the hunk made the docblock mixed. Same fix pass as 1.
3. `search-fields.test.ts` CONTROL comment: "`lookup` becomes an `$icontains`" could carry "single-valued" like the docblock does, since a `multiple: true` lookup takes the membership branch.

Check-runs on the head at review time: 15 success, 0 failure, 36 in_progress (Test Core, Test UI, Type Check · workspace, the remaining lint families), 9 skipped. No gate family has refused the head; the running ones cannot be moved by a two-comment diff and a changeset, and the record stands on the diff and the cited code.
